rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
C = Q/V
C = ε₀A/d
U = ½CV²

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ treat "Energy of charged capacitor" as one blob → ✅ split into: energy of charged capacitor.  ·  ❌ state the rule without its limit → ✅ note when it applies / stops applying.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Capacitance C = Q/V; parallel-plate C = ε₀A/d (larger with dielectric: C = ε₀εᵣA/d).  ·  Energy stored U = ½CV² = Q²/2C.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: **Energy stored.** The work done charging a capacitor is stored as electrostatic energy U = ½CV² = Q²/2C = ½QV, where C is capacitance, Q the charge and V the potential difference.  ·  **Energy density.** The energy per unit volume between the plates is u = ½ε₀E²; the same expression gives the energy density of any electric field in vacuum.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Series: 1/C = Σ1/C (same Q); Parallel: C = ΣC (same V).

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: **Charging a capacitor.** A battery of emf V supplies energy QV while charging, but only half (½QV) is stored — the rest is dissipated as heat in the circuit resistance.  ·  **Sharing between capacitors.** When a charged capacitor shares charge with an uncharged one, total charge is conserved but energy is lost as heat until the potentials equalise.  ·  **Applications.** Stored capacitor energy drives camera flashes, defibrillators and pulsed lasers, where energy must be released very rapidly.
